messages:
Leah Ortiz: Heads-up: were standardizing OIDC client IDs and deprecating personal access tokens for service automation. Goal: reduce scattered credentials and improve traceability. Migration window: Tue May 12 22:00-02:00 UTC. Docs: https://internal.redwood/security/oidc-client-migration-2026. Please review if you own any automation that uses PATs or custom OIDC client ids.

Marco Chen: Quick Q: will old PAT-based flows be cut immediately or supported with a short grace period? Some infra jobs rely on PATs to clone repos and push tags.

Leah Ortiz: Grace period: PAT token auth for service accounts will be accepted for 14 days after the cutover, but we will log and emit warnings. After 14 days they will be refused. Well publish a list of known service accounts and owners for rotation.

build-bot: preflight checks: github-app-perms -> PASS, oidc-issuers -> PASS, pat-usage-detection -> WARNING (23 service accounts found with PATs). See /debug/pat-list-1809009999.

Anika Bose: DevEx: we'll need a helper to exchange PATs for OIDC tokens and register new client IDs. I'll add a CLI: `redwood auth migrate-service --org $ORG --svc $NAME` which will: 1) create OIDC client, 2) update secrets in Vault, 3) patch CI pipeline to use OIDC. Drop PRs to devex/cli today.

Theo Grant: Ops: for runners that still need PATs (legacy deployers), we can provision short-lived machine identities using SSH certs or a delegated service account. Also planning to rotate webhook secrets during the migration window; expect ~30s webhook delivery hiccup.

Leah Ortiz: Security plan: enable enhanced logging (auth.client_id, auth.credential_type) and add an alert if failed_auth_rate > 1% over 10m. Rollback: flip idp-client-toggle to previous mapping and re-enable PAT acceptance for affected orgs. Steps in the runbook under "emergency-rollback".

Marco Chen: Nice. For Git operations, will the OIDC flow support git push via HTTPS with an access token? We need non-interactive git for releases.

Anika Bose: Yes — we'll issue short-lived Git tokens via the OIDC exchange that conform to the same scopes as current PATs. Example exchange snippet:
```
# exchange OIDC assertion for short-lived git token
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood/token \
  -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange \
  -d subject_token=<OIDC_ASSERTION> -d client_id=<NEW_CLIENT_ID>
```
Returned token TTL = 1h by default. We can extend per-org if needed.

build-bot: migration job scheduled: migrations/oidc-client-1809009999. Smoke tests: oidc-git-push -> PASS, oidc-ci-login -> PASS.

Theo Grant: I'll coordinate the webhook secret rotation and post the rotation commands here. Also tagging @oncall-auth for the cutover.

Leah Ortiz: Thanks all. Please subscribe to the runbook and fill the service-owner spreadsheet in the doc. We'll hold a short demo Tues 14:00 PT to walk through the migration CLI and answer questions. If you hit blockers, paste logs here. :wave:
